task.description:
WF-03 Step 2: Produce fix design for the pg.zig stderr logging issue.

Issue: pg.zig prints every PostgreSQL server error to stderr (e.g. `std.debug.print("POSTGRES ERROR: ...\n", ...)`). zig test runner treats stderr output as binary-level failure. Negative tests that DELIBERATELY trigger server errors abort the entire binary before their expectError assertion runs.

Required fix design:
- Silence pg.zig's server-error stderr logging by default.
- Provide a build flag (e.g. `-Dlog-pg-errors`) so developers can opt back into the old behavior for debugging.
- Do NOT remove the error from the return value of exec() — callers still need error.ServerError to propagate.

Produce a Type E prose design at `src/design/iss0607-pg-stderr-suppression.md` with:
- Problem statement (5 lines max)
- Approach: how to detect the build flag at compile time
- Public API impact (none expected — same ConnectOptions, same return types)
- File-by-file change list with exact function names and line ranges in vendor/pg/pg.zig
- Test plan: new regression test + how existing tests behave
- Risks and mitigations

DO NOT write implementation code. DO NOT modify vendor/pg/pg.zig. ONLY write the design markdown.

Run `python tools/lint_design_artefact.py src/design/iss0607-pg-stderr-suppression.md` and confirm exit 0.

Complete handoff with PASS.
acceptance_criteria: No implementation code in the design

result.summary: Type E prose design for the pg.zig stderr-on-server-error fix. One stderr site (vendor/pg/pg.zig:316) is gated behind a new build flag -Dlog-pg-errors wired through the existing build_options module. No public API change; PgError.ServerError still propagates unchanged. Test plan: new regression test that provokes a CHECK constraint violation and asserts expectError(error.ServerError, ...), plus all existing negative-path integration tests run reliably end-to-end.
